skill.name: mapreduce
skill.description: The MapReduce skill guides AI agents through parallel planning, implementation, and debugging workflows across Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and external provider CLIs. It then helps consolidate outputs with documented reducer patterns, file conventions, and scoring rubrics.
skill.summary: Run parallel AI workstreams and merge their outputs into one plan, implementation, or debugging decision.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline backticks. The confirmed issues are external CLI examples and shell prompt-construction patterns that can run provider tools and send task context outside the local environment. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent and data-handling warnings before Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode commands.
Avoid full-auto mode in marketplace examples, or gate it behind clear confirmation and sandbox guidance.
Replace command substitutions and interpolated shell strings with prompt files or clearly documented quoting rules.
Keep executable examples narrow and label code fences clearly to reduce scanner ambiguity.

static_findings.snippet: - `should handle concurrent updates` - race condition in update
- `should validate email format` - missing email regex
- Complex algorithms with multiple valid solutions
# Quick validation - check files are non-empty and valid TS
- Complex features with multiple valid approaches
| Hybrid | security | Best of both | Complexity |
- Use priority criteria: Feasibility > Risk > Completeness
| Type errors | tsc/mypy | Correctness -1 per error |

content.value_statement: Single-agent work can miss useful alternatives or defects. This skill fans work out to multiple agents or providers, then reduces their outputs into one decision.
actual_capabilities: Defines map, collect, and reduce phases for parallel agent workflows.
Shows patterns for planning, implementation comparison, and debugging consensus.
Documents reducer roles for plans, code, and debug findings.
Specifies output file conventions for plans, implementations, diagnoses, and consolidated results.
Includes scoring rubrics for comparing plans, code, and bug fixes.
Demonstrates optional external provider CLI usage for Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode.
limitations: It is guidance only; it does not ship the referenced reducer agent files in this package.
External CLI examples require installed provider tools and configured credentials.
Parallel outputs still need human review before code is merged or deployed.
The examples may send prompts or project details to third-party AI providers.

use_cases.title: Compare Implementation Options
use_cases.description: Generate competing implementations, run validation, and choose the safest merge path.

use_cases.title: Plan High-Risk Features
use_cases.description: Collect conservative, aggressive, security, and scalability plans before committing to a roadmap.

use_cases.title: Triangulate Bug Fixes
use_cases.description: Gather separate diagnoses, compare evidence, and select a minimal verified fix.

prompt_templates.title: Plan With Three Perspectives
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan {feature} with three workers: conservative, aggressive, and security. Ask each worker to write to a separate file. Consolidate into {output_path}.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementations
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate two or three implementation options for {feature}. Validate each option with the same tests. Reduce them into one selected approach and rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Build Debug Consensus
prompt_templates.prompt: Send {bug_report} to multiple diagnostic workers. Require evidence, likely root cause, and proposed fix. Reduce results into one verified repair plan.

prompt_templates.title: Run Multi-Provider Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a MapReduce review for {project_area}. Use Claude, Codex, or Claude Code only where approved. Compare outputs with security and maintainability weighted highest.

output_examples.input: Plan user authentication with conservative, aggressive, and security perspectives.
output_examples.output: A consolidated roadmap names accepted sections, rejected trade-offs, main risks, and next actions.

output_examples.input: Compare three generated user service implementations.
output: A merge plan identifies tests and fixes.

output_examples.input: Diagnose intermittent checkout failures across three workers.
output_examples.output: A verified root-cause summary lists the minimal fix path and confidence notes.

best_practices: Keep prompts scoped and tell each worker where to write its output.
Review external provider prompts for secrets before running CLI commands.
Set reducer criteria before starting so outputs can be compared fairly.
anti_patterns: Do not send sensitive source, credentials, or customer data to external providers without approval.
Do not accept a reducer decision without running tests or reviewing evidence.
Do not run several agents against the same files without isolated output paths.

faq.question: Does this skill run code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions; automation depends on the agent and tools you choose.

faq.question: Can it use Claude and Codex together?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents Claude subagents and Codex CLI patterns for parallel work.

faq.question: Does it require external provider accounts?
faq.answer: Only if you use optional CLI providers such as Codex, Gemini, Cursor, or OpenCode.

faq.question: How are results consolidated?
faq.answer: A reducer compares worker outputs using stated criteria and writes one selected or merged result.

faq.question: Is it safe for private code?
faq.answer: Use caution. External CLI examples can send prompts or code context outside your environment.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare a clear task, output paths, comparison criteria, and approval for any external tools.
